source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אַל־תִּירָ֣א וְאַל־תֵּחָ֔ת קַ֣ח עִמְּךָ֗ אֵ֚ת כָּל־עַ֣ם הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְק֖וּם עֲלֵ֣ה הָעָ֑י רְאֵ֣ה׀נָתַ֣תִּי בְיָדְךָ֗ אֶת־מֶ֤לֶךְ הָעַי֙ וְאֶת־עַמּ֔וֹ וְאֶת־עִיר֖וֹ וְאֶת־אַרְצֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Joshua, do not fear and do not be dismayed; take with you all [the] people of the war, and arise, go up [to] Ai; see, I have given into your hand the king of Ai and his people and his city and his land.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Take with you all the people of war, and arise, go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai and his people and his city and his land.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid or lose heart. Take the whole army with you and go up against Ai. See, I have handed the king of Ai over to you, with his people, his city and his land.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid. Do not lose courage. Take all your soldiers with you and go up to attack Ai. Look, I have put the king of Ai under your power, along with his people, his city and his land.

decisions.choice: do not fear and do not be dismayed: the encouragement God gave at the start, spoken again after the defeat
decisions.reason: The same pair of words comes in God's charge to Joshua (1:9) and in Moses' words to him (Deuteronomy 31:8). After the defeat at Ai and the sin of Achan (chapter 7), God renews the promise that he is with Joshua.

decisions.choice: all the people of war: the whole fighting force
decisions.reason: "People of war" means the men who go out to fight. The word "all" is pointed: the first attack used only about three thousand men because the spies said the whole army was not needed (7:3-4).

decisions.choice: I have given into your hand: a promise spoken as already done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for completed action, though the battle has not yet been fought, as in 6:2. "Into your hand" means into your power.

decisions.choice: the whole army (Balanced); all your soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: "People of war" is a Hebrew way of naming the army; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary English words.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ לָעַ֜י וּלְמַלְכָּ֗הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֤יתָ לִֽירִיחוֹ֙ וּלְמַלְכָּ֔הּ רַק־שְׁלָלָ֥הּ וּבְהֶמְתָּ֖הּ תָּבֹ֣זּוּ לָכֶ֑ם שִׂים־לְךָ֥ אֹרֵ֛ב לָעִ֖יר מֵאַחֲרֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will do to Ai and to its king just as you did to Jericho and to its king; only its spoil and its livestock you will plunder for yourselves. Set for yourself an ambush for the city from behind it.

en.L: And you shall do to Ai and to its king just as you did to Jericho and to its king; only its spoil and its livestock you may take as plunder for yourselves. Set for yourself an ambush against the city, behind it."
en.B: Do to Ai and its king what you did to Jericho and its king, except that this time you may take its spoil and its livestock as plunder for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city."
en.R: Do the same thing to Ai and its king that you did to Jericho and its king. But this time you may keep the goods and the animals for yourselves. Have some of your men hide behind the city, ready to attack it."

decisions.choice: only its spoil and its livestock for yourselves: at Ai the goods may be kept
decisions.reason: At Jericho everything was devoted to the LORD, and the people were to take nothing (6:17-19). Achan took from it anyway and brought disaster (7:1, 21). At Ai God himself allows Israel to keep the goods and the animals; the people and the city are still to be destroyed, as at Jericho (6:21, 24).

decisions.choice: an ambush: a force hidden near the city, waiting to strike
decisions.reason: The word is a participle meaning "one lying in wait". It names the men who hide and wait for the signal to attack (verses 4, 19).

decisions.choice: behind it: on the side away from the main army
decisions.reason: The main army comes at the city from the north (verse 11); "behind" is the west side, where the ambush is placed (verses 9, 12).

decisions.choice: this time
decisions.reason: The word "only" sets Ai against Jericho. Balanced and Readable add "this time" to make the contrast with Jericho plain.

decisions.choice: Have some of your men hide behind the city, ready to attack it
decisions.reason: Readable explains what an ambush is instead of using the word.

source.text: וַיָּ֧קָם יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ וְכָל־עַ֥ם הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה לַעֲל֣וֹת הָעָ֑י וַיִּבְחַ֣ר יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים אֶ֤לֶף אִישׁ֙ גִּבּוֹרֵ֣י הַחַ֔יִל וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֖ם לָֽיְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Joshua and all [the] people of the war to go up [to] Ai; and chose Joshua thirty thousand men, mighty [men] of valor, and sent them by night.

en.L: And Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up to Ai; and Joshua chose 30,000 men, mighty [men] of valor, and sent them out by night.
en.B: So Joshua and the whole army set out to go up against Ai. Joshua chose 30,000 of his best fighting men and sent them off at night.
en.R: So Joshua and all his soldiers got ready to attack Ai. Joshua chose 30,000 of his bravest fighters and sent them out at night.

decisions.choice: arose: set out, got moving
decisions.reason: "Arise" here is not only standing up but starting to act, the answer to God's "arise, go up" in verse 1.

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor: tried and capable warriors
decisions.reason: The phrase names strong, experienced fighting men, as in 1:14. These are the best of the army, chosen for the hidden attack.

decisions.choice: thirty thousand men: the number of the chosen force; verse 12 gives five thousand for the ambush
decisions.reason: Verse 12 says Joshua set about five thousand men in ambush. The two numbers may describe two groups (a larger chosen force and the ambush itself), or verse 12 may tell the same step again with a different count. The word for "thousand" can also name a military unit, as noted at Numbers 1:21, which would make the numbers smaller. The text does not settle the question.

decisions.choice: his best fighting men (Balanced); his bravest fighters (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Mighty men of valor" is kept at Literal; Balanced and Readable say in plain words what kind of men they were.

source.text: וַיְצַ֨ו אֹתָ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר רְ֠אוּ אַתֶּ֞ם אֹרְבִ֤ים לָעִיר֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י הָעִ֔יר אַל־תַּרְחִ֥יקוּ מִן־הָעִ֖יר מְאֹ֑ד וִהְיִיתֶ֥ם כֻּלְּכֶ֖ם נְכֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he commanded them, saying, see, you [are] lying in ambush for the city from behind the city; do not go far from the city very, and you will be, all of you, ready.

en.L: And he commanded them, saying, "See, you are to lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, and be ready, all of you.
en.B: He gave them these orders: "Listen. You are to lie in wait against the city from behind it. Do not go very far from the city, and all of you be ready.
en.R: He gave them these orders: "Listen carefully. You must hide behind the city and wait to attack it. Do not go very far from it. All of you be ready.

decisions.choice: see: pay attention
decisions.reason: "See" at the start of an order calls the hearers to attend to what follows.

decisions.choice: you are lying in ambush: the task they are given
decisions.reason: The verb is a participle, describing their position and role from now on: they are to be the hidden force.

decisions.choice: Listen (Balanced); Listen carefully (Readable)
decisions.reason: In English a call for attention is "listen" rather than "see".

source.text: וַאֲנִ֗י וְכָל־הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתִּ֔י נִקְרַ֖ב אֶל־הָעִ֑יר וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־יֵצְא֤וּ לִקְרָאתֵ֨נוּ֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּרִֽאשֹׁנָ֔ה וְנַ֖סְנוּ לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I and all the people who [are] with me will draw near to the city; and it will be, when they come out to meet us as at the first, and we will flee before them,

en.L: And I and all the people who [are] with me will draw near to the city. And it will be, when they come out to meet us as at the first [time], that we will flee before them.
en.B: I will advance on the city with all the troops who are with me. When its men march out to fight us, just as before, we will turn and run from them.
en.R: I will go toward the city with all the rest of the army. The men of Ai will come out to fight us, as they did the first time, and we will run away from them.

decisions.choice: come out to meet us: come out to fight us
decisions.reason: To "meet" an army is to go out against it in battle, as in verse 14.

decisions.choice: as at the first: as in the first attack
decisions.reason: The men of Ai came out and drove the Israelites back the first time (7:4-5). Joshua plans to use their confidence against them.

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); the rest of the army (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The people" here are the fighting men with Joshua, as distinct from the ambush.

source.text: וְיָצְא֣וּ אַחֲרֵ֗ינוּ עַ֣ד הַתִּיקֵ֤נוּ אוֹתָם֙ מִן־הָעִ֔יר כִּ֣י יֹֽאמְר֔וּ נָסִ֣ים לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר בָּרִֽאשֹׁנָ֑ה וְנַ֖סְנוּ לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will come out after us until we have drawn them from the city, for they will say, [they are] fleeing before us as at the first; and we will flee before them.

en.L: And they will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, 'They are fleeing before us as at the first [time].' And we will flee before them.
en.B: They will come after us until we have drawn them away from the city, because they will think, 'They are running from us just as before.' So we will keep running from them.
en.R: They will chase us until we have led them away from the city. They will think, 'They are running away from us, just like last time.' So we will keep running.

decisions.choice: drawn them away: pulled them out, lured them
decisions.reason: The verb means to pull or tear away. The same verb in verse 16 says the plan worked: the men of Ai "were drawn away from the city".

decisions.choice: they will say: they will tell themselves
decisions.reason: "Say" here is what the men of Ai will think as they see Israel run.

decisions.choice: So we will keep running
decisions.reason: The second "we will flee" says the flight goes on while the enemy follows. English shows that with "keep running".

source.text: וְאַתֶּ֗ם תָּקֻ֨מוּ֙ מֵהָ֣אוֹרֵ֔ב וְהוֹרַשְׁתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הָעִ֑יר וּנְתָנָ֛הּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will rise from the ambush and take possession of the city, and will give it Yahweh your God into your hand.

en.L: And you will rise up from the ambush and take possession of the city, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will give it into your hand.
en.B: Then you will rise from your hiding place and seize the city. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will hand it over to you.
en.R: Then you must come out of hiding and take the city. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will give it to you.

decisions.choice: take possession of: seize and hold
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for taking possession of the land. Here it means to take the city and hold it.

decisions.choice: the LORD your God will give it into your hand: the victory is God's gift
decisions.reason: The plan is a soldier's plan, but the outcome depends on God, as he promised in verse 1 and says again in verse 18.

decisions.choice: your hiding place (Balanced); come out of hiding (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The ambush" here is the place where the men lie hidden, so Balanced and Readable name it as a hiding place.

source.text: וְהָיָ֞ה כְּתָפְשְׂכֶ֣ם אֶת־הָעִ֗יר תַּצִּ֤יתוּ אֶת־הָעִיר֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ רְא֖וּ צִוִּ֥יתִי אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when you have seized the city, you will set fire [to] the city with fire; according to the word of Yahweh you will do. See, I have commanded you.

en.L: And it will be, when you have seized the city, you shall set fire to the city with fire; according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} you shall do. See, I have commanded you."
en.B: As soon as you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said. Those are my orders to you."
en.R: When you have captured the city, set it on fire. Do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has told you. Those are my orders."

decisions.choice: set fire to the city, according to the word of the LORD: Ai is to be treated as Jericho was
decisions.reason: God told Joshua to do to Ai what he had done to Jericho (verse 2), and Jericho was burned (6:24). The fire is also the signal the main army will see (verses 20-21).

decisions.choice: See, I have commanded you: a closing formula
decisions.reason: These words end the orders and give them their full weight: this is a command, not advice.

decisions.choice: Those are my orders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the closing formula the way English ends a set of orders.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֣ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ אֶל־הַמַּאְרָ֔ב וַיֵּשְׁב֗וּ בֵּ֧ין בֵּֽית־אֵ֛ל וּבֵ֥ין הָעַ֖י מִיָּ֣ם לָעָ֑י וַיָּ֧לֶן יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַה֖וּא בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent them Joshua, and they went to the ambush and stayed between Bethel and between Ai, west of Ai; and spent the night Joshua in that night in [the] midst of the people.

en.L: And Joshua sent them out, and they went to the [place of] ambush and stayed between Bethel and Ai, on the west of Ai; and Joshua spent that night in the midst of the people.
en.B: Then Joshua sent them off. They went to their hiding place and waited between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai, while Joshua spent that night with the army.
en.R: Then Joshua sent them on their way. They went to the place where they would hide, between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai. Joshua spent that night in the camp with the rest of the army.

decisions.choice: between Bethel and Ai: the ground west of Ai, toward Bethel
decisions.reason: Bethel lay a short distance west of Ai (7:2 places Ai east of Bethel). The ambush hid in the hill country between the two towns, out of sight of Ai.

decisions.choice: west: literally "from the sea"
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel the sea, the Mediterranean, lies to the west, so "seaward" is the ordinary Hebrew word for west.

decisions.choice: the people: here the main army that stayed with Joshua
decisions.reason: "The people" in this chapter often means the fighting men (verses 1, 3, 5). Joshua stayed with the main force, not with the ambush.

decisions.choice: in the camp with the rest of the army
decisions.reason: Readable says where Joshua was and who "the people" were.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֤ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּפְקֹ֖ד אֶת־הָעָ֑ם וַיַּ֨עַל ה֜וּא וְזִקְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לִפְנֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם הָעָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose early Joshua in the morning and mustered the people, and went up he and [the] elders of Israel before the people [to] Ai.

en.L: And Joshua rose early in the morning and mustered the people, and he went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.
en.B: Early the next morning Joshua mustered the troops, and he and the elders of Israel led them up to Ai.
en.R: Early the next morning Joshua called the soldiers together and counted them. Then he and the elders of Israel led them up to Ai.

decisions.choice: mustered: called up and reviewed the troops
decisions.reason: The verb means to call to account, to number or inspect. Before a battle it means to gather the soldiers and see that all are present and ready.

decisions.choice: the elders of Israel: the heads of the tribes and families
decisions.reason: The elders went with Joshua at the head of the army. After the defeat at Ai they had mourned with him before the ark (7:6).

decisions.choice: led them up
decisions.reason: "Went up before the people" means they went at the head of the army; Balanced and Readable say "led them".

source.text: וְכָל־הָעָ֨ם הַמִּלְחָמָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֗וֹ עָלוּ֙ וַֽיִּגְּשׁ֔וּ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ נֶ֣גֶד הָעִ֑יר וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ מִצְּפ֣וֹן לָעַ֔י וְהַגַּ֖י בֵּינָ֥יו וּבֵין־הָעָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And all the people of the war who [were] with him went up and approached and came before the city, and camped north of Ai, and the valley [was] between him and Ai.

en.L: And all the people of war who [were] with him went up and drew near and came in front of the city, and they camped on the north of Ai, and the valley [was] between him and Ai.
en.B: All the fighting men with him went up, drew near and arrived in front of the city. They camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and the town.
en.R: All the soldiers with him went up and came close to the city. They set up camp on the north side of Ai, with a valley between them and the town.

decisions.choice: between him and Ai: "him" is Joshua with his army
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular, but it stands for Joshua and the force he leads, camped as one body.

decisions.choice: the valley: a ravine on the north side of Ai
decisions.reason: The camp was in plain sight of the city across the valley. That drew the eyes of Ai to the north while the ambush waited to the west.

decisions.choice: between them and the town
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "them" for Joshua and his army, as English does for a group.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֕ח כַּחֲמֵ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים אִ֑ישׁ וַיָּ֨שֶׂם אוֹתָ֜ם אֹרֵ֗ב בֵּ֧ין בֵּֽית־אֵ֛ל וּבֵ֥ין הָעַ֖י מִיָּ֥ם לָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took about five thousand men and set them [as] an ambush between Bethel and between Ai, west of the city.

en.L: And he took about 5,000 men and set them [as] an ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the west of the city.
en.B: He took about 5,000 men and posted them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
en.R: Joshua took about 5,000 men and had them hide between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city.

decisions.choice: about five thousand men: the size of the ambush
decisions.reason: Verse 3 speaks of thirty thousand chosen men; see the note there on how the two numbers relate.

decisions.choice: verses 12-13 kept as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation is shorter here and does not have verses 12-13, which retell the setting of the ambush and the camp. The Hebrew text is followed. Reviewers should check this against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: Readable names Joshua instead of "he".

source.text: וַיָּשִׂ֨ימוּ הָעָ֜ם אֶת־כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ מִצְּפ֣וֹן לָעִ֔יר וְאֶת־עֲקֵב֖וֹ מִיָּ֣ם לָעִ֑יר וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַה֖וּא בְּת֥וֹךְ הָעֵֽמֶק׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set the people, all the camp which [was] north of the city and its rear west of the city; and went Joshua in that night into [the] midst of the valley.

en.L: And they set the people, all the camp that [was] north of the city, and its rear guard west of the city; and Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley.
en.B: So the troops took their positions: the main camp north of the city and the rear guard west of it. That night Joshua went down into the middle of the valley.
en.R: So the army was in place. The main camp was north of the city, and the men in hiding were to the west. That night Joshua went down into the middle of the valley.

decisions.choice: its rear guard: literally "its heel", the force at the back
decisions.reason: The word means "heel" and so the rear of a body of troops. Here it is the ambush to the west of the city.

decisions.choice: they set the people: the army was put in position
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; the sense is that the troops were set in their places, the main camp and the ambush.

decisions.choice: went: Joshua went into the valley that night
alternatives: spent the night in the middle of the valley
decisions.reason: Some Hebrew manuscripts read "spent the night" in the valley, a very similar word, as in verse 9. The standard Hebrew text reads "went", and that is followed here.

decisions.choice: the men in hiding
decisions.reason: Readable names the rear guard by what it was, the ambush.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י כִּרְא֣וֹת מֶֽלֶךְ־הָעַ֗י וַֽיְמַהֲר֡וּ וַיַּשְׁכִּ֡ימוּ וַיֵּצְא֣וּ אַנְשֵֽׁי־הָעִ֣יר לִקְרַֽאת־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל לַֽמִּלְחָמָ֞ה ה֧וּא וְכָל־עַמּ֛וֹ לַמּוֹעֵ֖ד לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽעֲרָבָ֑ה וְהוּא֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע כִּֽי־אֹרֵ֥ב ל֖וֹ מֵאַחֲרֵ֥י הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when saw [the] king of Ai, and hurried and rose early and went out the men of the city to meet Israel for the battle, he and all his people, to the appointed place before the Arabah; and he did not know that an ambush [was] for him from behind the city.

en.L: And it came about, when the king of Ai saw [it], that the men of the city hurried and rose early and went out to meet Israel for battle, he and all his people, at the appointed place facing the Arabah; but he did not know that [there was] an ambush against him behind the city.
en.B: When the king of Ai saw this, he and all his people, the men of the city, hurried out early to meet Israel in battle at the place set for it, facing the Arabah. He did not know that an ambush was waiting for him behind the city.
en.R: When the king of Ai saw the Israelites, he and all his army hurried out early in the morning to fight them. They went to the place set for the battle, facing the Jordan Valley. But he did not know that men were hiding behind the city, ready to attack him.

decisions.choice: when the king of Ai saw: what he saw is not stated
decisions.reason: The context implies that he saw the Israelite camp across the valley to the north (verse 11).

decisions.choice: the appointed place: a set place for the battle
decisions.reason: The word means a fixed time or a fixed place. Here it is probably a place chosen for the battle, perhaps where Ai had met Israel before. It could also mean "at the appointed time".

decisions.choice: the Arabah: the deep valley of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the rift valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea, east of Ai and far below it. The battle was on the side of Ai that faced it.

decisions.choice: the Jordan Valley
decisions.reason: Readable uses a name that tells young readers where the Arabah is.

decisions.choice: saw the Israelites; men were hiding ... ready to attack him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the king saw and explains the ambush.

source.text: וַיִּנָּֽגְע֛וּ יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And let themselves be struck Joshua and all Israel before them, and fled [by the] way of the wilderness.

en.L: And Joshua and all Israel let themselves be struck before them and fled by the way of the wilderness.
en.B: Joshua and all Israel pretended to be beaten by them and fled toward the wilderness.
en.R: Joshua and all the Israelites acted as if they were losing, and they ran away toward the desert.

decisions.choice: let themselves be struck: they made it look as if they were being beaten
decisions.reason: The verb is in a form that can mean "allow oneself to be struck". The retreat was part of the plan (verses 5-6), not a real defeat.

decisions.choice: the way of the wilderness: the road toward the dry country to the east
decisions.reason: The wilderness here is the dry land falling away from Ai toward the Jordan valley, away from the city and the hidden ambush.

decisions.choice: pretended to be beaten (Balanced); acted as if they were losing (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that the defeat was staged.

source.text: וַיִּזָּעֲק֗וּ כָּל־הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּעַ֔י לִרְדֹּ֖ף אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיִּרְדְּפוּ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ וַיִּנָּתְק֖וּ מִן־הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And were called together all the people who [were] in Ai to pursue after them, and they pursued after Joshua and were drawn away from the city.

en.L: And all the people who [were] in Ai were called out to pursue after them; and they pursued after Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
en.B: All the people in Ai were called out to chase them. They pursued Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
en.R: All the men in Ai were called out to chase the Israelites. As they chased Joshua, they were led farther and farther from the city.

decisions.choice: in Ai
decisions.reason: The letters written in the standard Hebrew text read "in the city"; the reading the scribes marked to be read aloud is "in Ai". Both mean the same place.

decisions.choice: were drawn away: the plan of verse 6 worked
decisions.reason: This is the verb Joshua used in verse 6, "until we have drawn them away from the city".

decisions.choice: the Israelites; farther and farther
decisions.reason: Readable names those being chased and shows the men of Ai being pulled away step by step.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־נִשְׁאַ֣ר אִ֗ישׁ בָּעַי֙ וּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יָצְא֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּעַזְב֤וּ אֶת־הָעִיר֙ פְּתוּחָ֔ה וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And not remained a man in Ai and Bethel who did not go out after Israel; and they left the city open and pursued after Israel.

en.L: And not a man remained in Ai and Bethel who did not go out after Israel; and they left the city open and pursued after Israel.
en.B: Not one man stayed behind in Ai or Bethel; every one of them went out after Israel. They left the city wide open as they chased Israel.
en.R: Every man in Ai and Bethel went out after the Israelites. They left the city wide open and chased them.

decisions.choice: and Bethel: the men of Bethel joined in the chase
decisions.reason: Bethel was the next town to the west (verse 9). Its men came out with the men of Ai, and so the ambush between the two towns was left unseen. The king of Bethel is named among the kings Israel defeated (12:16).

decisions.choice: and Bethel kept as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation does not have "and Bethel" here. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: open: unguarded, its gates left open
decisions.reason: No one stayed to defend the city, so the ambush could walk in (verse 19).

decisions.choice: Every man ... went out
decisions.reason: Readable says positively what the Hebrew says with two negatives.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ נְ֠טֵה בַּכִּיד֤וֹן אֲשֶׁר־בְּיָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל־הָעַ֔י כִּ֥י בְיָדְךָ֖ אֶתְּנֶ֑נָּה וַיֵּ֧ט יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ בַּכִּיד֥וֹן אֲשֶׁר־בְּיָד֖וֹ אֶל־הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Joshua, stretch out the javelin which [is] in your hand toward Ai, for into your hand I will give it. And stretched out Joshua the javelin which [was] in his hand toward the city.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Stretch out the javelin that [is] in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand." And Joshua stretched out the javelin that [was] in his hand toward the city.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Hold out the javelin in your hand toward Ai, for I will hand the city over to you." So Joshua held out the javelin in his hand toward the city.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Point the spear in your hand toward Ai. I will give that city to you." So Joshua pointed his spear toward the city.

decisions.choice: javelin: a short spear, or possibly a curved sword
decisions.reason: The word names a weapon carried in the hand. It is often taken as a javelin, and some take it as a curved sword. Either way it is held up high as a sign.

decisions.choice: stretch out toward Ai: the signal for the ambush and a sign of God's power
decisions.reason: The raised weapon was the signal for the ambush (verse 19), and Joshua kept it raised until Ai was destroyed (verse 26), as Moses kept his hands raised in the battle with Amalek (Exodus 17:11-12).

decisions.choice: into your hand I will give it: the promise placed first for weight
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "into your hand" first, stressing that the city will be given to Joshua.

decisions.choice: spear
decisions.reason: Readable uses the common word "spear" for a javelin.

source.text: וְהָאוֹרֵ֡ב קָם֩ מְהֵרָ֨ה מִמְּקוֹמ֤וֹ וַיָּר֨וּצוּ֙ כִּנְט֣וֹת יָד֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ הָעִ֖יר וַֽיִּלְכְּד֑וּהָ וַֽיְמַהֲר֔וּ וַיַּצִּ֥יתוּ אֶת־הָעִ֖יר בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the ambush rose quickly from its place, and they ran as he stretched out his hand, and they came [into] the city and captured it, and hurried and set fire [to] the city with fire.

en.L: And the ambush rose quickly from its place, and they ran as soon as he stretched out his hand, and they entered the city and captured it; and they hurried and set fire to the city with fire.
en.B: As soon as he held out his hand, the men in ambush rose quickly from their position and ran forward. They entered the city, captured it and quickly set it on fire.
en.R: As soon as Joshua held out his hand, the men who were hiding jumped up and ran into the city. They captured it and quickly set it on fire.

decisions.choice: as he stretched out his hand: the moment of the signal
decisions.reason: The ambush moved the moment Joshua raised the javelin. His hand and the javelin are the same gesture (verse 26).

decisions.choice: the ambush ... they ran: one group, then many men
decisions.reason: "The ambush" is a single word for the whole hidden force, so the first verb is singular, and the following verbs are plural for the men in it.

decisions.choice: As soon as he held out his hand, ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the signal first so that the order of events is clear.

source.text: וַיִּפְנ֣וּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ הָעַ֨י אַחֲרֵיהֶ֜ם וַיִּרְא֗וּ וְהִנֵּ֨ה עָלָ֜ה עֲשַׁ֤ן הָעִיר֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יְמָה וְלֹא־הָיָ֨ה בָהֶ֥ם יָדַ֛יִם לָנ֖וּס הֵ֣נָּה וָהֵ֑נָּה וְהָעָם֙ הַנָּ֣ס הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר נֶהְפַּ֖ךְ אֶל־הָרוֹדֵֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And turned the men of Ai behind them and saw, and look, went up [the] smoke of the city to the heavens, and there were not in them hands to flee here or there; and the people that fled [to] the wilderness turned back against the pursuer.

en.L: And the men of Ai turned behind them and looked, and see, the smoke of the city was going up to the heavens, and there was no strength in them to flee this way or that way; and the people who were fleeing to the wilderness turned back against the pursuers.
en.B: The men of Ai looked back and saw the smoke of their city rising into the sky. They had no chance to escape in any direction, and the Israelites who had been running toward the wilderness turned around against their pursuers.
en.R: The men of Ai looked back. They saw smoke from their city rising up into the sky. They had no way to get away. The Israelites who had been running toward the desert turned around to fight the men chasing them.

decisions.choice: no hands to flee: no power or room to escape
decisions.reason: "Hand" often means power or strength. The men of Ai were caught between the burning city and the army that had turned to face them.

decisions.choice: see: the word marks a sudden sight
decisions.reason: The word draws the reader into what the men of Ai saw as they turned.

decisions.choice: the people who were fleeing: the Israelite army
decisions.reason: These are Joshua's men, who had pretended to flee (verse 15). "The pursuer" is singular in Hebrew for the whole force of Ai.

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people who were fleeing, so they are not taken for the men of Ai.

source.text: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ וְכָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל רָא֗וּ כִּֽי־לָכַ֤ד הָֽאֹרֵב֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר וְכִ֥י עָלָ֖ה עֲשַׁ֣ן הָעִ֑יר וַיָּשֻׁ֕בוּ וַיַּכּ֖וּ אֶת־אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And Joshua and all Israel saw that had captured the ambush the city and that went up [the] smoke of the city, and they turned back and struck the men of Ai.

en.L: And Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city was going up, and they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.
en.B: Joshua and all Israel saw the smoke going up from the city and knew that the ambush had captured it. Then they turned back and attacked the men of Ai.
en.R: Joshua and all the Israelites saw that their men had captured the city and that it was burning. So they turned around and fought the men of Ai.

decisions.choice: the smoke of the city: the sign that the plan had worked
decisions.reason: The smoke told the men of Ai that their city was lost (verse 20) and told Israel that the ambush had done its part.

decisions.choice: struck: attacked and began to cut down
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike, and in battle to attack or kill. Verse 22 tells how the fight ended.

decisions.choice: their men; it was burning
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the ambush" and the smoke.

source.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה יָצְא֤וּ מִן־הָעִיר֙ לִקְרָאתָ֔ם וַיִּֽהְי֤וּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בַּתָּ֔וֶךְ אֵ֥לֶּה מִזֶּ֖ה וְאֵ֣לֶּה מִזֶּ֑ה וַיַּכּ֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם עַד־בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־ל֖וֹ שָׂרִ֥יד וּפָלִֽיט׃

records.literal_gloss: And these came out from the city to meet them, and they were to Israel in the middle, these from this [side] and these from this [side]; and they struck them until not was left to him a survivor or a fugitive.

en.L: And these came out from the city to meet them, and they were in the middle of Israel, some on this side and some on that side; and they struck them down until there was not left to them a survivor or a fugitive.
en.B: The men of the ambush came out of the city against them, so the men of Ai were caught in the middle, with Israelites on both sides. Israel struck them down until not one survivor or fugitive was left.
en.R: The Israelites in the city came out to fight them too. So the men of Ai were trapped in the middle, with Israelites on both sides. The Israelites killed them all. No one got away, and no one was left alive.

decisions.choice: these ... these: the ambush coming from the city and the main army
decisions.reason: The first "these" are the men of the ambush, who came out of the burning city. The men of Ai were then caught between them and Joshua's army.

decisions.choice: survivor or fugitive: no one at all
decisions.reason: A survivor is one left alive; a fugitive is one who escapes. Together the two words mean that none of the fighting men of Ai lived.

decisions.choice: the men of the ambush / the Israelites in the city; the men of Ai
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses only "these" and "them". Balanced and Readable name each group so that the reader can follow the battle.

source.text: וְאֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ הָעַ֖י תָּ֣פְשׂוּ חָ֑י וַיַּקְרִ֥בוּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻֽׁעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the king of Ai they seized alive and brought him near to Joshua.

en.L: And the king of Ai they seized alive, and they brought him to Joshua.
en.B: But they seized the king of Ai alive and led him to Joshua.
en.R: But they caught the king of Ai alive and took him to Joshua.

decisions.choice: the king of Ai alive: the one exception
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "the king of Ai" first, setting him apart from the men who all fell (verse 22). What becomes of him is told in verse 29.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: The fronted object sets the king against the rest; Balanced and Readable show the contrast with "but".

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י כְּכַלּ֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל לַהֲרֹג֩ אֶת־כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֨י הָעַ֜י בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר רְדָפ֣וּם בּ֔וֹ וַֽיִּפְּל֥וּ כֻלָּ֛ם לְפִי־חֶ֖רֶב עַד־תֻּמָּ֑ם וַיָּשֻׁ֤בוּ כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הָעַ֔י וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֹתָ֖הּ לְפִי־חָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when had finished Israel to kill all [the] inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness where they had pursued them in it, and had fallen all of them by [the] mouth of [the] sword until they were finished, and returned all Israel [to] Ai and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword.

en.L: And it came about, when Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness where they had pursued them, and they had all fallen by the edge of the sword until they were finished, that all Israel returned to Ai and struck it with the edge of the sword.
en.B: When Israel had finished killing all the people of Ai in the open country and in the wilderness where they had chased them, and every one of them had fallen by the sword until none were left, all Israel went back to Ai and put it to the sword.
en.R: The Israelites killed all the people of Ai who were out in the open country and in the desert where they had chased them. Every one of them was killed with the sword. Then all the Israelites went back to Ai and killed the people there with the sword.

decisions.choice: by the mouth of the sword: by the edge of the sword, in battle
decisions.reason: The edge of the sword is called its "mouth", the part that devours. The phrase means killing in battle.

decisions.choice: the field, the wilderness: the open land outside the city
decisions.reason: "Field" is the open country around a town, as against the town itself. The fighting men of Ai died out there, where they had chased Israel.

decisions.choice: struck it: struck the city, those still inside
decisions.reason: "It" is Ai itself, meaning the people left in the city, men and women (verse 25).

decisions.choice: by the sword
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the edge of the sword"; Balanced and Readable say "by the sword" or "with the sword", as English does.

source.text: וַיְהִי֩ כָל־הַנֹּ֨פְלִ֜ים בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ מֵאִ֣ישׁ וְעַד־אִשָּׁ֔ה שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר אָ֑לֶף כֹּ֖ל אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, all those falling on that day, from man and to woman, twelve thousand, all [the] people of Ai.

en.L: And all who fell on that day, from man to woman, were 12,000, all the people of Ai.
en.B: On that day 12,000 fell, men and women alike, the whole population of Ai.
en.R: That day 12,000 men and women died. That was everyone who lived in Ai.

decisions.choice: from man to woman: men and women alike, everyone
decisions.reason: The phrase sets two ends to include everyone between them.

decisions.choice: all the people of Ai: the whole population
decisions.reason: The word is "men of Ai", but here it plainly includes the women, so it means the people of the town.

decisions.choice: twelve thousand
decisions.reason: The total includes the town as well as its fighting men. On the word "thousand" see the note at verse 3.

source.text: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ לֹֽא־הֵשִׁ֣יב יָד֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָטָ֖ה בַּכִּיד֑וֹן עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱרִ֔ים אֵ֖ת כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָעָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And Joshua did not draw back his hand which he stretched out with the javelin until he had devoted to destruction all [the] inhabitants of Ai.

en.L: And Joshua did not draw back his hand that he had stretched out with the javelin until he had devoted to destruction all the inhabitants of Ai.
en.B: Joshua did not lower the hand that held out his javelin until he had devoted all the people of Ai to destruction.
en.R: Joshua kept holding out his spear until he had completely destroyed all the people of Ai, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction: given over wholly to the LORD by being destroyed
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for Jericho (6:17, 21). What is "devoted" is taken out of human use and handed over to God, here by death, as commanded in Deuteronomy 20:16-17.

decisions.choice: did not draw back his hand: like Moses' raised hands
decisions.reason: Joshua kept the javelin raised until the end, as Moses held up his hands until Amalek was defeated (Exodus 17:11-12). The raised hand shows that the victory came from God.

decisions.choice: verse 26 kept as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation does not have this verse. The Hebrew text is followed. Reviewers should check this against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: completely destroyed ..., as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word as the other books do (Deuteronomy 2:34), so that the reader sees that this was an act given over to God, not ordinary killing.

decisions.choice: spear
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

source.text: רַ֣ק הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וּשְׁלַל֙ הָעִ֣יר הַהִ֔יא בָּזְז֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖ה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻֽׁעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Only the livestock and the spoil of that city plundered for themselves Israel, according to the word of Yahweh which he commanded Joshua.

en.L: Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Israel took as plunder for themselves, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had commanded Joshua.
en.B: Israel kept for themselves only the livestock and the spoil of that city, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Joshua.
en.R: The Israelites kept only the animals and the goods from the city for themselves. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Joshua to do.

decisions.choice: only the livestock and the spoil: as God allowed in verse 2
decisions.reason: Israel took exactly what God had allowed and no more. The care stands against Achan's theft at Jericho (7:21).

decisions.choice: spoil: the goods taken from a defeated city
decisions.reason: The word covers the goods, clothing and valuables carried off after a battle.

decisions.choice: Israel kept for themselves only ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "only the livestock and the spoil" first. Balanced and Readable start with Israel, as English does.

source.text: וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ אֶת־הָעָ֑י וַיְשִׂימֶ֤הָ תֵּל־עוֹלָם֙ שְׁמָמָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned Joshua Ai and made it a mound of forever, a desolation, until this day.

en.L: And Joshua burned Ai and made it a mound forever, a desolation, until this day.
en.B: So Joshua burned Ai and left it a ruin mound for all time, a desolate place, as it still is today.
en.R: Joshua burned Ai and left it a heap of ruins forever. It is still an empty ruin today.

decisions.choice: a mound: the heap left by a ruined town
decisions.reason: Towns in the land were rebuilt again and again on the same spot, and a ruined town became a hill of rubble. The name Ai itself sounds like a word for a heap of ruins (Micah 3:12 uses that word).

decisions.choice: a mound forever: the fate Deuteronomy gives a city devoted to destruction
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 13:17 says such a city "shall be a mound forever" and never be rebuilt.

decisions.choice: until this day: until the time the book was written
decisions.reason: The writer tells his readers that they can still see the ruin.

source.text: וְאֶת־מֶ֧לֶךְ הָעַ֛י תָּלָ֥ה עַל־הָעֵ֖ץ עַד־עֵ֣ת הָעָ֑רֶב וּכְב֣וֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ֩ צִוָּ֨ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וַיֹּרִ֧ידוּ אֶת־נִבְלָת֣וֹ מִן־הָעֵ֗ץ וַיַּשְׁלִ֤יכוּ אוֹתָהּ֙ אֶל־פֶּ֨תַח֙ שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֔יר וַיָּקִ֤ימוּ עָלָיו֙ גַּל־אֲבָנִ֣ים גָּד֔וֹל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And the king of Ai he hanged on the tree until [the] time of the evening; and at [the] going of the sun commanded Joshua, and they took down his corpse from the tree and threw it at [the] entrance of [the] gate of the city, and raised over him a heap of stones, great, until this day.

en.L: And the king of Ai he hanged on the tree until evening time; and at the going down of the sun Joshua commanded, and they took his corpse down from the tree and threw it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and they raised over him a great heap of stones, until this day.
en.B: He hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset Joshua gave the order, and they took the body down from the tree and threw it down at the entrance of the city gate. They raised over it a large heap of stones, which is there to this day.
en.R: Joshua hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening. When the sun went down, Joshua gave orders to take the body down. They threw it down at the entrance of the city gate and piled a large heap of stones over it. That pile of stones is still there today.

decisions.choice: hanged on the tree: the body of the king put on show
decisions.reason: In 10:26 Joshua first kills five kings and then hangs them on trees, and that is probably what happens here: the king's body is displayed as a sign of his defeat. The text does not say how he was put to death.

decisions.choice: at sunset they took the body down: the law of Deuteronomy 21:22-23
decisions.reason: The law says that the body of one hung on a tree must not stay there all night. Joshua keeps that law even for an enemy king.

decisions.choice: a great heap of stones: a marker, as over Achan
decisions.reason: A great heap of stones was raised over Achan too (7:26). The gate of the city, where the king had ruled and judged, became the place of his grave.

decisions.choice: the body
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "corpse". Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable say "the body".

source.text: אָ֣ז יִבְנֶ֤ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּהַ֖ר עֵיבָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Then built Joshua an altar to Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, on [the] mountain of Ebal,

en.L: Then Joshua built an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,
en.B: Then Joshua built an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,
en.R: Then Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: an altar on Mount Ebal: what Moses commanded in Deuteronomy 27
decisions.reason: Moses told Israel to set up plastered stones with the law written on them on Mount Ebal, to build an altar of uncut stones there, and to offer sacrifices (Deuteronomy 27:2-8; see also 11:29). Verses 30-35 tell how Joshua did it.

decisions.choice: Mount Ebal: the northern of the two mountains at Shechem
decisions.reason: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim face each other across the valley of Shechem, well to the north of Ai. The text does not tell how Israel came there.

decisions.choice: verses 30-35 placed here, after the taking of Ai
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation places these verses after 9:2, and a fragment of Joshua found among the Dead Sea Scrolls places this event near the crossing of the Jordan, before 5:2. The standard Hebrew text, followed here, places it after the victory at Ai.

decisions.choice: then: at that time
decisions.reason: "Then" with this verb form introduces something done in that period, without fixing the day.

decisions.choice: to worship the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what the altar was for.

source.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּה֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּכָּתוּב֙ בְּסֵ֨פֶר֙ תּוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֔ה מִזְבַּח֙ אֲבָנִ֣ים שְׁלֵמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־הֵנִ֥יף עֲלֵיהֶ֖ן בַּרְזֶ֑ל וַיַּעֲל֨וּ עָלָ֤יו עֹלוֹת֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּזְבְּח֖וּ שְׁלָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: just as had commanded Moses, [the] servant of Yahweh, the sons of Israel, as [is] written in [the] book of [the] law of Moses, an altar of whole stones on which not had wielded [anyone] iron; and they offered up on it burnt offerings to Yahweh and sacrificed peace offerings.

en.L: just as Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, as [it is] written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of whole stones on which no one had wielded iron. And they offered burnt offerings on it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and sacrificed peace offerings.
en.B: following the command that Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, as the book of the law of Moses records: an altar of uncut stones that no iron tool had touched. On it they offered burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and sacrificed peace offerings.
en.R: He did this as Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, had told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to do. It is written in the book of Moses' teaching. The altar was made of stones from the field, just as they were, and no one had used iron tools to cut them. On it they offered burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they also offered peace offerings.

decisions.choice: whole stones, no iron: the altar law of Deuteronomy 27:5-6 and Exodus 20:25
decisions.reason: Moses commanded an altar of whole stones, left uncut, with no iron tool swung on them (Deuteronomy 27:5-6), as the first altar law says (Exodus 20:25). Joshua builds it in exactly that way.

decisions.choice: the book of the law of Moses: the written teaching Moses gave
decisions.reason: Moses wrote down the law and gave it to the priests (Deuteronomy 31:9, 24). "Law" here is the whole of Moses' teaching, not only its rules, as at Deuteronomy 1:5.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and peace offerings
decisions.reason: Burnt offerings were burned whole on the altar; peace offerings were shared in a meal before the LORD. Both were commanded for this altar (Deuteronomy 27:6-7).

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The title of Moses follows the rule for this word, as at 1:1.

decisions.choice: uncut stones, iron tool (Balanced); stones from the field, just as they were, iron tools to cut them (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording matches the command in Deuteronomy 27:5-6, so the reader can see that it was carried out to the letter.

source.text: וַיִּכְתָּב־שָׁ֖ם עַל־הָאֲבָנִ֑ים אֵ֗ת מִשְׁנֵה֙ תּוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּתַ֔ב לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he wrote there on the stones a copy of [the] law of Moses which he had written before [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And he wrote there on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: There, in the presence of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the law of Moses.
en.R: There, while the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} watched, Joshua wrote a copy of the law of Moses on the stones.

decisions.choice: a copy: a second writing of the law
decisions.reason: The word means a repetition or copy. Deuteronomy 17:18 uses it of the copy of the law the king must write for himself.

decisions.choice: which he wrote before the sons of Israel: Joshua wrote it with Israel looking on
alternatives: which Moses had written for the sons of Israel
decisions.reason: "He" is most naturally Joshua, writing in the sight of the people. It could also be Moses, who had written the law for Israel (Deuteronomy 31:9).

decisions.choice: the stones: the stones Deuteronomy 27 commanded
decisions.reason: Moses told Israel to set up large stones, coat them with plaster, and write on them all the words of the law (Deuteronomy 27:2-4, 8). The text does not say whether these are the altar stones or separate ones.

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Joshua as the writer, following the reading in the note above.

source.text: וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל וּזְקֵנָ֡יו וְשֹׁטְרִ֣ים׀וְשֹׁפְטָ֡יו עֹמְדִ֣ים מִזֶּ֣ה׀וּמִזֶּ֣ה׀לָאָר֡וֹן נֶגֶד֩ הַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים הַלְוִיִּ֜ם נֹשְׂאֵ֣י׀אֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֗ה כַּגֵּר֙ כָּֽאֶזְרָ֔ח חֶצְיוֹ֙ אֶל־מ֣וּל הַר־גְּרִזִ֔ים וְהַֽחֶצְי֖וֹ אֶל־מ֣וּל הַר־עֵיבָ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֜ה מֹשֶׁ֣ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֗ה לְבָרֵ֛ךְ אֶת־הָעָ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּרִאשֹׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And all Israel and its elders and officials and its judges [were] standing on this [side] and on this [side] of the ark before the priests, the Levites, carriers of [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh, the sojourner as the native, half of it toward [the] front of Mount Gerizim and the half of it toward [the] front of Mount Ebal, just as had commanded Moses, [the] servant of Yahweh, to bless the people Israel at the first.

en.L: And all Israel, and its elders and officials and its judges, were standing on this side and on that side of the ark, in front of the priests, the Levites, who carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the sojourner as well as the native, half of them in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, just as Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded at the first, to bless the people Israel.
en.B: All Israel, with its elders, officials and judges, stood on both sides of the ark, facing the Levitical priests who carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Outsiders stood there as well as native Israelites. Half of them stood facing Mount Gerizim and half facing Mount Ebal. Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded this earlier, so that the people of Israel would be blessed.
en.R: All the Israelites stood on both sides of the ark, facing the priests from the tribe of Levi who carried the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant. Their elders, officials and judges were there, and so were the outsiders living among them as well as those born Israelites. Half of the people stood facing Mount Gerizim, and the other half faced Mount Ebal. This was what Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, had told them to do earlier, so that the people of Israel would receive the blessing.

decisions.choice: half before Mount Gerizim and half before Mount Ebal: the command of Deuteronomy 27
decisions.reason: Moses ordered six tribes to stand on Mount Gerizim for the blessing and six on Mount Ebal for the curse, with the Levites speaking (Deuteronomy 11:29; 27:11-14).

decisions.choice: the sojourner as well as the native: outsiders living among Israel stood with them
decisions.reason: A sojourner is someone from another people who lives among Israel without family land of his own. The covenant ceremony included them (Exodus 12:38; Deuteronomy 29:10; 31:12).

decisions.choice: at the first: Moses' command given earlier
alternatives: to bless the people of Israel first
decisions.reason: The phrase may go with "commanded", meaning Moses had given the command earlier, or with "to bless", meaning the blessing came first, before the curse (verse 34).

decisions.choice: officials and judges: the men who kept order and settled disputes
decisions.reason: The officials carried out orders for the leaders (1:10; 3:2), and the judges heard cases (Deuteronomy 16:18).

decisions.choice: sojourner (Literal); outsiders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for a resident foreigner follows the choice of Leviticus and Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 31.

source.text: וְאַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן קָרָא֙ אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י הַתּוֹרָ֔ה הַבְּרָכָ֖ה וְהַקְּלָלָ֑ה כְּכָל־הַכָּת֖וּב בְּסֵ֥פֶר הַתּוֹרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And after thus he read all [the] words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all the written in [the] book of the law.

en.L: And after that he read all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the law.
en.B: After that, Joshua read aloud all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, just as they are written in the book of the law.
en.R: After that, Joshua read aloud every word of the teaching, both the blessing and the curse, just as they are written in the book of the teaching.

decisions.choice: the blessing and the curse: the two ways set before Israel
decisions.reason: Moses set before Israel a blessing for obeying and a curse for turning away (Deuteronomy 11:26-29; 27:12-26; 28:1-68). Joshua reads them both in the land itself.

decisions.choice: read: read aloud, proclaim
decisions.reason: The verb means to call out, and with a book to read aloud to hearers, as Deuteronomy 31:11 commands.

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Joshua.

decisions.choice: the teaching
decisions.reason: Readable uses "teaching" for the law of Moses, as Deuteronomy does at Readable.

source.text: לֹֽא־הָיָ֣ה דָבָ֔ר מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־קָרָ֜א יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ נֶ֣גֶד כָּל־קְהַ֤ל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְהַנָּשִׁ֣ים וְהַטַּ֔ף וְהַגֵּ֖ר הַהֹלֵ֥ךְ בְּקִרְבָּֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Not was a word of all that had commanded Moses which not read Joshua before all [the] assembly of Israel, and the women and the little ones and the sojourner who was going in their midst.

en.L: There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua did not read before all the assembly of Israel, and the women and the little ones, and the sojourner who went along in their midst.
en.B: There was not a single word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua did not read aloud before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women and children and the outsiders who lived among them.
en.R: Joshua read every single word that Moses had commanded. He read it to the whole gathering of Israel: the men, the women, the children, and the outsiders who lived among them.

decisions.choice: the assembly, the women, the little ones, the sojourner: the hearers Deuteronomy 31:12 names
decisions.reason: Moses commanded that the law be read to the men, the women, the little ones and the sojourner, so that all could hear and learn to fear the LORD (Deuteronomy 31:12). Joshua's reading includes them all.

decisions.choice: going in their midst: living and traveling with them
decisions.reason: To "go" among a people is to live among them, sharing their life on the march.

decisions.choice: not a word ... that Joshua did not read: every word was read
decisions.reason: The two negatives make a strong positive: nothing Moses commanded was left out.

decisions.choice: Joshua read every single word
decisions.reason: Readable says positively what the Hebrew says with two negatives.

decisions.choice: the men
decisions.reason: Readable names the men alongside the women and children, since the assembly here means the gathered men of Israel.
